name: Marúbo
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Costa, Raquel G. R. (2000) Aspectos da fonologia Marubo (Pano): uma visao nao-linear. PhD thesis, UFRJ (also Costa 1992, Padroes ritmicos e marcacao de caso em Marubo)

new_statements.quote: Tipologicamente, o Marubo é uma sistema acentual misto entre o acento morfológico e o acento rítmico. No nível da palavra, o acento recai sobre uma sílaba da raiz (geralmente a primeira) e os sufixos se submetem a esse acento. No nível do sintagma e da sentença, o acento ocorre a intervalos regulares de distância. [...] A grande maioria das palavras simples em Marubo é constituída de dissílabos com acento na primeira sílaba, como em (24a). Segue-se a eles uma quantidade razoável de dissílabos com acento na segunda sílaba (24b). Há uma pequena quantidade de trissílabos com acento na primeira sílaba (25a) e, com menor freqüência, na segunda (25b). Monossílabos são raros (23).
new_statements.translation: Typologically, Marubo is a mixed system between morphological stress and rhythmic stress. At the word level, stress falls on a syllable of the root (generally the first) and the suffixes submit to that stress. At the phrase and sentence level, stress occurs at regular intervals. [...] The great majority of simple words in Marubo are disyllables with stress on the first syllable, as in (24a). Next comes a fair number of disyllables with stress on the second syllable (24b). There is a small number of trisyllables with stress on the first syllable (25a) and, less frequently, on the second (25b). Monosyllables are rare (23).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word (lexical) stress is root-bound and by default root-/word-initial: syllabic trochees built left to right with End Rule Left, quantity-insensitive (light and heavy syllables behave alike). A lexically listed minority of roots are iambs with stress on the second syllable (e.g. ku'ki 'basket', ka'pɨ 'caiman', ya'wiʃi 'armadillo'). Suffixes never take the word stress; pronominal proclitics lean on the host and are outside the count. Main phonetic correlate is high pitch; duration and intensity follow from it.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Above the word, a ternary left-to-right rhythm builds a non-adjacent trochee; in domains of five or more syllables the 4th syllable receives the phrasal accent by End Rule Right, and Costa transcribes this phrasal accent as the strongest prominence (»») with the lexical root stress as secondary (») in such long words/phrases, e.g. nu»ku-ka»»ɾaN-katsa 'will arrive'. Four-syllable words have only the initial foot.
new_statements.exceptions: Lexically marked iambic roots (2nd-syllable stress), a 'quantidade razoável' of disyllables and a few trisyllables; rare stressed monosyllables (degenerate feet); ergative (also locative/instrumental/genitive) case marking on disyllabic nouns inverts prominence (trochee <-> iamb) together with final-vowel nasalization; some verb roots invert stress between transitive and intransitive use; a few formatives (causative, motion/direction) have their own rhythmic autonomy; monosyllabic function words lose stress in connected speech. Smith 2021 adds that nasalized syllables typically attract stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is for the prosodic word = root + suffixes (proclitics excluded), citation and context forms from one speaker of São Sebastião (rio Curuçá). Word-level peak is leftmost; phrase-level peak is rightmost, so in words of 5+ syllables or in phrases the strongest prominence is the phrasal accent, not the lexical one.
new_statements.identity_note: All three Costa works describe Marubo of the Vale do Javari (rios Ituí and Curuçá); Costa 2002 states all data come from one speaker (Pa»nan) of the São Sebastião community on the rio Curuçá. Kennell's FUNAI ms calls the language 'Marúbo (Chainawa)'. Same languoid as maru1252; no dialect split is reported.

sources.citation: Smith, C. Sean. 2021. Aspects of Switch Reference in Marubo, a Panoan Language of Western Amazonia. MA thesis, Trinity Western University. 114 pp.
sources.note: p.8 (brief phonology/orthography note): 'In general, primary stress falls on the first syllable of the word, but nasalized syllables typically attract stress. Any variation to this basic pattern is indicated by an acute accent, which is also used to mark secondary stress.'

sources.citation: González, Carolina. 2017. Tipología de los sistemas métricos de veinticinco lenguas Pano. Amerindia 39(1): 129-172.
sources.note: Second-hand survey: Marubo classed '5.1 Inicial, No cohesivo' after Costa (2000, 2002); lexical stress normally on first root syllable, less often second; syllabic trochee default with lexically marked iambs; phrasal accent on 4th syllable (pp.154-155).

sources.note: No per-language stress statement for Marubo (classification/bibliography only).

sources.citation: Costa, Raquel Guimarães Romankevicius. 2002. Interações entre restrições em Marubo (Pano). Revista da ABRALIN 1(1): 11-34. DOI 10.25189/rabralin.v1i1.727
sources.note: Sec.2 pp.17-30: 'No nível da palavra, o acento principal recai sobre a margem esquerda: na primeira sílaba em palavras trocaicas e na segunda sílaba em palavras iâmbicas' (p.26); trochee default, iamb lexically marked (MAX-stress-IO >> RhType=T); words of 5+ syllables carry a stronger (phrasal) accent on the 4th syllable; phrasal peak rightmost (RIGHTMOST-PhP), lexical peak leftmost; note 6: stress = high pitch + greater duration and intensity.

sources.note: Sec.4 (pp.105-107) Marubo: 'O padrão mais geral e básico é '-.... raízes com duas sílabas, sendo a primeira alta, longa e tônica. Também há raízes nas quais a segunda sílaba é proeminente'; trisyllabic roots mostly first-syllable prominent; formatives (suffixes) mostly rhythmically neutral.

sources.citation: Costa, Raquel G. R. 1992. Padrões rítmicos e marcação de caso em Marubo (Pano). Dissertação de Mestrado, UFRJ. 289 pp. (UFRJ Pantheon hdl 11422/3194; Wayback copy)
sources.note: Ch.2 and conclusions pp.250-257: five rhythmic patterns for simple roots; the most general are binary '-. and ternary '-.. (first syllable high, long, tonic), followed by.'- and.'-.; monosyllabic pattern rare; pitch height is the main correlate; each word has one prominent syllable; rhythmic regulation operates left to right; at most one initial non-prominent syllable per word.
